g.text: Bacterial Cell Structure and Gram Staining
Today we are looking at bacterial cell structure, starting with the cell membrane.
The cell membrane consists primarily of a phospholipid bilayer, and it controls what moves into and out
Now, gram-positive bacteria have a thick peptidoglycan layer. This distinction is going to be on the
exam, so make sure you remember it.
Gram-negative bacteria, by contrast, have a much thinner peptidoglycan layer plus an outer membrane
